findings.source_quote: καὶ ἀνεκαίνισεν ἡμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ ἤδη κατεφθαρμένων ἡμῶν καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων ἐλπίδα τοῦ ζῆν ἀνενέωσε τὴν ζωὴν ἡμῶν.
findings.english_quote: He renewed our spirit and our life[c] when we were already ruined and had no hope of living.
findings.issue: Combining the two renewal clauses makes the condition of being already ruined and without hope of living modify both the renewal of spirit and the renewal of life. The selected Greek states the renewal of spirit separately, then attaches that condition to the renewal of life. The simplified wording thus extends the condition beyond its stated attachment and obscures the two distinct renewal assertions.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “He renewed our spirit. When we were already ruined and had no hope of living, he renewed our life.[c]”

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all six paragraphs of the selected Greek. The standard edition preserves the clauses, conditions, negations, speaker changes, and difficult assertions. The simplified edition needs correction to the scope of the condition accompanying renewal in paragraph 3. The disclosed bracketed supplements and foundation alternative do not require replacing the working readings. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify external editions, or establish exhaustive collation. The proposed correction requires fresh review.
